- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes in sentiment; apply a 2–5 day lag correction to avoid overshoot after spikes.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses downward trends in low-sentiment periods; add a 1–3% downward bias if sentiment < 0.2 for 3+ consecutive days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -1.0 → +1.0), model tends to mispredict direction; use sentiment momentum as a filter for directionality.
